nodes.label: F1 — epoch-unqualified Role-B write-backs, made racy by the Restart path
nodes.rationale: Write-backs key on peer id only, never on pending_epoch or new_tun. Before dc3d0bb the contains_key guard meant an entry was never replaced while it existed; RoleBDecision::Restart removes and re-inserts, destroying that invariant — so done/cut_over land on the wrong epoch's entry and the collapse arm orphans a live Device+enforcer that nothing will ever collapse.

nodes.label: F2 — the live_enforcers gauge cannot express the alert it was written for
nodes.rationale: A displacing insert leaves map.len() unchanged and the real signal is 'N tuns, N-1 enforcers' with N unexported; deferred because exporting live_tunnels needs a channel out of the non-Send run task, which is the same structural rework the endpoint/port fix will do.

nodes.label: F3 — new_epoch_watch_keys re-enters the stall through its fallback
nodes.rationale: Falling back to the snapshot for 'no key selected' watches a key the device provably does not hold, so all_live is false every tick and the old Device and enforcer are never torn down — exactly what 5a5f644 was written to prevent, re-entered one branch over. Latent today but fixed anyway, because it is the precise drift the function exists to make impossible.

nodes.label: F4 — all_live vacuously true when the watch set empties
nodes.rationale: Genuinely ambiguous: if the peers really left, retiring is correct; if rot.desired is transiently truncated, retiring destroys a key live peers still need.

nodes.label: F5 — MAX_ROTATION_TUNS = 64 is an undocumented fabric-size ceiling
nodes.rationale: The comment justifies 64 as far beyond any plausible fan-out, which is true per-rotation but not per-fabric under the in-step design; the failure is a per-peer eprintln + continue with no metric, after which affected peers take the rule-4 grace-promote onto a key that was never established.

nodes.label: F6 — plan_ifname reuses the lowest free slot, making F1 deterministic
nodes.rationale: Tunnel::up waits only for the UAPI socket to appear, and a not-yet-unlinked socket from the dropped Device satisfies that instantly; tear_down only logs an ip link del failure. Fix: monotonic or quarantined slot allocation.

nodes.label: TunnelId e/o namespace split is structural, not probabilistic
nodes.rationale: plan_ifname cannot produce the same name for an Own and an Overlap for any input, and the boot port is excluded structurally by starting at offset 1 rather than by a check that could be forgotten.
